identificationModule.briefTitle: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Systems in People With Type 2 Diabetes Not Treated With Insulin
identificationModule.officialTitle: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Systems in People With Type 2 Diabetes Not Treated With Insulin - the Association With Metabolic Control of Diabetes and Markers of Early Vascular Changes

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The aim of the study is to assess the influence of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems on metabolic control and quality of life in people with type 2 diabetes and overweight/obesity who are not treated with insulin. Additionally, the study aims to assess the association between metabolic control of diabetes and markers of early cardiovascular disease, taking into account the impact of CGM use.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Pharmacological treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) has advanced significantly in recent years. However, despite increasing availability of new medications, a great proportion of patients do not achieve treatment goals, which leads to an increased risk of chronic complications. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems have become standard of care in persons with diabetes treated with insulin, although they might also be a useful tool in guiding behaviour and dietary choices in patients treated with non-insulin medications. However, the data on their potential benefits in people with T2DM not using insulin are scarce. Therefore, the study aims to investigate the influence of CGM use on metabolic control and quality of life in this group of patients.

The study subjects will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: using continuous glucose monitoring systems or performing self-monitoring of blood glucose with a glucose meter. The intervention time will be 12 weeks, with control visits every 4 weeks. A post-intervention follow-up visit to assess whether the achieved results are maintained will be performed at 3 months after completing the intervention.

armGroups.label: Continuous glucose monitoring
armGroups.description: Dexcom One+ continuous glucose monitoring system

interventions.name: Continuous glucose monitoring
interventions.description: Participants will be randomized to use Dexcom One+ continuous glucose monitoring system for 12 weeks, with control visits every four weeks.

interventions.name: Self-monitoring of blood glucose
interventions.description: Participants will be randomized to continue self-monitoring of blood glucose with a glucose meter as per usual practice, with control visits every four weeks.

primaryOutcomes.description: Observed change in time in range (70-180 mg/dl) from baseline to week 12 in the group using CGM system compared to the group using SMBG.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Observed change in the percentage of glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) from baseline to week 12.
Observed change in time in tight range (TITR; 70-140 mg/dl) from baseline to week 12.
Observed change in time above range (TAR; \>180 mg/dl) from baseline to week 12.
Observed change in time below range (TBR; \<70 mg/dl) from baseline to week 12.
Observed change in glycaemic variability assessed with coefficient of variation (CV) from baseline to week 12.
Observed change in body weight from baseline to week 12.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in markers of early vascular disease
secondaryOutcomes.description: Observed change in the concentrations of circulating markers of subclinical vascular disease: oxLDL, VCAM-1, ICAM-1, E-selectin, interleukin 6, interleukin 18 from baseline to week 12.

Observed change in diabetes distress measured with DDS questionnaire from baseline to week 12.

DDS is a 17-item questionnaire assessing diabetes distress over the previous month. Scores \<2 points indicates no/little distress, 2-2.9 points - moderate distress, and ≥3 points - high distress.

Observed change in Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score from baseline to week 12.

PHQ-9 is a 9-item questionnaire for screening, diagnosing, monitoring and measuring the severity of depression. Total score: 0-27 points; higher scores reflect greater severity of depressive symptoms.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in quality of life: WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire
secondaryOutcomes.description:
Observed change in abbreviated World Health Organization Quality of Life (WHOQOL-BREF) questionnaire from baseline to week 12.

Total score: 0-100 points; higher scores reflect higher quality of life.

Observed change in sleep quality measured with Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) from baseline to week 12.

Total score: 0-21 points; a score greater than 5 indicates significant sleep difficulties.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age between 18 and 65 years (both inclusive)
* Type 2 diabetes diagnosed at least 6 months prior to entering the study
* Body mass index ≥25 kg/m2
* Diabetes treated with oral medications and/or GLP-1 receptor agonists and/or tirzepatide
* No modifications of diabetes treatment in the previous 3 months
* HbA1c between 7.5% and 10% (both inclusive)
* Oral and written informed consent for participation

Exclusion Criteria:

* Type 1 diabetes, gestational diabetes, other specific types of diabetes
* HbA1c \>10.0%
* Treatment with insulin
* Previous use of any continuous glucose monitoring system
* GFR \<30 ml/min
* Acute infections, acute diabetes complications and/or unplanned hospitalisations in the previous month
* Use of steroids or immunosuppressive medications in the previous 3 months
* Chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immune therapy in the previous 3 months
* Pregnancy and/or breastfeeding
* Skin lesions or dermatological conditions preventing proper sensor insertion
* Cognitive impairment and/or other conditions preventing proper use of continuous glucose monitoring system
* Lack of consent for the use of continuous glucose monitoring system
